name: CampaignBars – Announcement & Notification Bars
author: Plugins.shop

sections.description:
Add a WordPress announcement bar at the top or bottom of your website, without editing your theme. Announce a launch, explain a delivery deadline, share a coupon code or link to an offer. Choose where and when each message appears.

Free, not a trial. Create unlimited campaigns with no account, API key, required paid service, time limit or forced public branding. WooCommerce is not required.

Try it before installing

Try the Free demo | Try the Pro demo

Explore the workspace with fictional data, not your live site. Pro is a separate paid add-on, not included in Free.

What you can do with Free

  • Announcement and notification bars: templates, messages and buttons linking to your pages, offers or forms.
  • Sticky top or fixed bottom placement: colors, offsets and shorter mobile text to fit your site.
  • Countdown timers: a fixed deadline for launches, events or promotions; not a visitor-specific evergreen timer.
  • Copyable coupon codes: copying does not create, validate or apply a discount.
  • Page and audience targeting: page, page-type, device and login rules. Exclusions win; WooCommerce checkout and a page with the exact slug checkout are excluded by default. Add any other checkout page to Exclusions.
  • Scheduled announcements: site-timezone start/end dates, dismissal and once-per-session display.
  • Preview before publishing: separate drafts, an illustrative editor preview and expiring, publisher-only previews on real pages.
  • Campaign management: search, filter, duplicate, pause, resume and recover trashed campaigns. Restore one of 20 revisions as a draft.
  • Optional local reports: approximate views/clicks, not unique-person counts, and last-30-days CSV export. Measurement is off by default; configure consent first.

One eligible bar appears at a time. Editors gain no automatic publishing permission.

When Pro is useful

Pro adds advanced campaign tools and WooCommerce shipping progress based on store rules, eligible coupon application and purchase attribution. Attribution does not prove additional sales.

Explore Pro | Compare Free and Pro

Hideable Pro examples in Free activate no paid features. Local Pro needs no key; eligible licences control private downloads/updates. Install Free before compatible Pro.

Useful alongside CampaignBars

Made by Plugins.shop. Useful companions for the next step after someone notices your announcement:

  • KillerConversions – WordPress contact forms — Link your button to a contact, quote or enquiry form.
  • ClickClue – WordPress session replay — Review eligible landing-page visits using its recording and privacy controls.
  • OrderFloor – WooCommerce minimum order and quantity limits — Set purchasing rules your bars explain. Requires WooCommerce.

Separate, optional Plugins.shop tools with Free editions; none is required or installed automatically. Configure each separately. More plugins shows the locally bundled catalogue.

External services and APIs

Free makes no external API/licence/analytics/font/image requests. WordPress core handles directory/update/translation requests. Campaign display and measurement use your own site’s endpoints.

Consent connections read locally from installed WP Consent API, Cookiebot or custom JavaScript. No service is installed/contacted; availability alone grants no consent. Configure separately. Cookiebot: terms, privacy.

Clicked links open websites: CampaignBars privacy, terms, Plugins.shop privacy. The optional review link opens CampaignBars on WordPress.org; no review is posted automatically.

Privacy and data

Measurement defaults off; consent requirement defaults on. The browser waits for your configured analytics grant; the server receives a client-reported flag, not proof of consent or a human visit. Turning the requirement off allows counting without consent. Neither edition guarantees legal compliance.

Tab-session sessionStorage retains seen/dismissed state independently of analytics consent. Page dismissal follows the page/publication in the current tab; blocked storage or duplicated tabs can affect it. Free sets no visitor tracking cookie.

When measurement is enabled, abuse controls process the server-reported IP in memory and store daily salted hashes, not raw IPs. IPv6 uses /64; forwarded headers are not trusted. Shared networks and limits can omit counts; automation can still affect reports. These controls do not process IPs/write counters when measurement is off. Servers may keep separate logs.

Daily cleanup targets 90 site-calendar days of report aggregates; delayed jobs/deactivation can retain data longer. Campaigns, settings, editor IDs and revisions remain until removed. Exports/backups have separate retention.

After a successful publication, CampaignBars stores that publisher’s first publication time to wait 30 days before showing a review invitation on its Campaigns page. Only publishers on production sites see it. The timestamp and each publisher’s reminder or dismissal choice are local, per-site WordPress user preferences, exportable/erasable with WordPress privacy tools. No visitor tracking or automatic WordPress.org request is involved.

Deactivation/uninstall preserve data by default. Destructive Free uninstall is blocked while Pro remains installed; each multisite site’s deletion choice is respected. Opt-in removal excludes WooCommerce orders, Pro attribution, logs, backups and browser data.

Full endpoint, consent, retention, abuse-limit and deletion details are in documentation.txt. Suggested privacy text is in WordPress’s Privacy Policy Guide.

Source and license

Readable PHP/JS/CSS; no build or remote code loader. GPL-2.0-or-later: LICENSE.txt. Logos: assets/collection/SOURCES.txt. Technical reference: documentation.txt.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate CampaignBars via Plugins > Add New, or upload the Free ZIP.
  2. Choose a template and set your message, button, audience and dates.
  3. Save a draft, review preview/visibility checks, then publish.
  4. Configure measurement and consent in Settings if you want reports. This is not a consent banner; the private accept/revoke test grants no consent and records no measurements.
  5. Clear page/CDN caches and test your theme on desktop and mobile.

Before updating, back up the database/files and verify a restore on staging. Replace Free, then compatible Pro, without uninstalling. Old campaign-bars package? Follow the migration FAQ.

Getting started guide | Get support
sections.faq:
Can I use it without WooCommerce or a paid account?

Yes. Free needs neither WooCommerce nor an external account. It does not collect email addresses; a button can link to your signup or contact page.

Can I show different bars on different pages or on mobile?

Yes: use targeting rules and shorter mobile text. When several campaigns qualify, the highest eligible ID wins; editing does not reorder them. Pro adds priorities.

Why is my announcement bar not appearing?

Check publication, dates, rules, dismissal and frequency in visibility checks. Clear caches after changes or Pro activation/deactivation; blocked scripts/requests prevent display. Public-page discovery checks for new/resumed campaigns. Simulations cannot certify theme/CSS/cache delivery or inspect another visitor.

How do I migrate from the old campaign-bars package?

Back up. In OLD Free Settings, turn OFF Delete plugin data on uninstall; save and verify. Deactivate Pro then old Free. Delete old Free only with that setting off, or remove via SFTP without uninstalling. Install current Free then matching Pro; clear caches, verify data. Never activate both Free packages. Before WordPress 6.9, use the Plugins screen, not programmatic legacy activation. Read migration.txt first.
sections.changelog:
1.2.5

  • Refine checkout exclusions and campaign workspace feedback based on Free edition QA.
  • Keep the matched Pro add-on separate; update Free first without uninstalling.

1.2.4

  • Add a delayed, dismissible review invitation inside the CampaignBars workspace and an optional Help link to the WordPress.org reviews page.
  • Keep review preferences per publisher and per site, with privacy export/erase and opt-in uninstall cleanup. No visitor tracking or automatic external request.

1.2.3

  • Protect shared data when removing Free with Pro installed; respect each multisite site’s deletion choice.
  • Bound public measurement requests and deduplication storage, coalesce repeated counts and honor emergency pause.
  • Remember page-specific dismissals for the current tab and reject unsafe campaign links.
  • Preserve extension settings during saves and normalize migrated presentation fields without dropping inactive Pro configuration.

Earlier changes are in changelog.txt.
